question: Jaccard below 0.11 proved the model families are not text copies. It did not prove they need separate full executors. Can one LayerOp IR express a dense transformer and a recurrent state model?
why_rejected: It is the exact failure the campaign document names: indirection added without executor code deleted. The IR costs 2,250 lines to delete 480, functions rise from 154 to 170, and bit-exactness on argmax and top-k cannot be proven through the lowering. A graph that grows the tree and cannot guarantee the discrete decisions is not a condensation, whatever it does to conceptual tidiness.
first_precise_behaviour_contract: Dual sequence-mixer with dual state layout under identity-lowering: WKV-7's fixed per-head S state and token-shift cannot share one executable LayerOp core with a transformer's growing KV cache plus RoPE plus MHA while remaining bit-exact on argmax and top-k, holding one command buffer per token, and being net-negative in LOC.

qwen_dense.why: growing KV cache, GQA, RoPE and QKV bias are not expressible as a WKV recurrence
61 kernel calls across 19 Q4_K variants in the greedy TCB path, bit-identity bound
fusion boundaries already tuned for single-command-buffer encode

rwkv7.why: per-head fixed S[hs,hs] recurrence, O(1) state, no KV, no RoPE
previous-token shift state is not a KV slot; fresh-flag semantics differ
MLP and time-mix substructure do not match the SwiGLU transformer shape

significance: This settles the question both architecture scouts independently flagged as their first blocker, and it settles it against unification. The families are not merely different in source text -- they are different in state layout and sequence mixing, which is a semantic difference the previous jaccard measurement could not see and this analysis can. Programme 3 is closed.
lane_behaviour: Correct. It was instructed to reject its own design if the graph added indirection without deleting executors, and it did exactly that rather than reporting a conceptual win.
